text: This is yet another example of this President weaponizing the Department of Justice to target his critics and political opponents. It is a total abuse of power. Full stop. https://t.co/CK6aUkjnPx

quoted.text:
Just 22 days before the midterm Congressional elections, federal agents shockingly searched the D.C. home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, a sitting Democratic Member of Congress from Minnesota. According to public reporting, DHS’s laughable excuse for this assault on our constitutional values was that they were looking for fraud in immigration paperwork that Rep. Omar’s late father filled out several decades ago, when Rep. Omar was a child and the family came to America as refugees fleeing the civil war in Somalia.  Rep. Omar has been a naturalized American citizen for decades, and her constituents have overwhelmingly elected her to Congress four times. She has now been made the target of a classic Trump political harassment and frame-up operation during the last three weeks of a Congressional election in which President Trump describes himself as being ‘on the ballot.’
 
Federal agents appear to have searched a sitting congresswoman’s home not to investigate any real crime or threat, but to carry out a campaign of political retribution against one of President Trump’s most outspoken critics. This kind of presidential harassment and persecution of a political critic is exactly why the Framers wrote the Speech or Debate Clause and the First Amendment—to protect Members of Congress and citizens against petty and vindictive reprisal by the Executive branch.
 
DOJ violated its own policy, which requires the Department to abstain from overt actions in politically-sensitive matters in the 60 days before an election, to conduct this search. This is no accident. Just 22 days before the elections, this is blatant political intimidation and an attempt to interfere with the Congresswoman’s reelection. It is also the culmination of a smear campaign against Minnesota’s Somali American community.
 
Rep. Omar now joins the ranks of multiple Democratic Members of Congress who have been targeted by Trump’s vindictive Administration on the most outlandish trumped-up charges, including Rep. Maggie Goodlander, Rep. Jason Crow, Rep. Chris Deluzio, Rep. Chrissy Houlahan, Rep. LaMonica McIver, Senator Adam Schiff, Senator Elissa Slotkin, and Senator Mark Kelly. This DOJ routinely harasses Trump’s perceived enemies, including former FBI Director James Comey, New York Attorney General Letitia James and my constituent Davey Hearn, a three-time Olympic canoeist framed on utterly bogus charges for turning our Reflecting Pool into an algae farm, which was actually the handiwork of Trump’s $15 million no-bid pool contractor. In none of these cases has the Administration succeeded in doing anything other than wasting taxpayer resources and forcing citizens to waste their own precious time and money defending themselves against bogus charges.
 
House Judiciary Committee Democrats stand with Rep. Omar against this outrageous abuse of power, and we will be demanding transparency and accountability as to who authorized this abusive search and who carried it out.

text:
Yesterday, I was proud to highlight the impact of the TEXAS Grant and Federal Pell Grant programs in expanding access to higher education for students at TAMIU and Laredo College.

During my time in the Texas Legislature, I worked alongside State Senator Rodney Ellis to establish the TEXAS Grant Program, helping students with financial need pursue a college education. Since then, students at both institutions have
received more than $198.3 million in TEXAS Grant assistance and more than
$504.6 million in Pell Grants from 2014 through 2025.

Together, these programs represent more than $702.9 million in financial assistance, helping thousands of students across South Texas pursue their degrees and build brighter futures.

I remain committed to supporting programs that make higher education more affordable and expand opportunities for students and their families. I’ll continue working to ensure students at TAMIU, Laredo College and across South Texas have the resources they need to succeed.

quoted.text:
Serving as the United States Ambassador to Greece has been the honor of a lifetime. I will forever be grateful to President Donald J. Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio for entrusting me with the extraordinary privilege of representing the greatest country in the history of the world.

From my first day as Ambassador, I have worked tirelessly to advance President Trump’s America First agenda, strengthen our strategic alliance with Greece, and deliver meaningful victories for the American people.

During my tenure, we have helped secure historic agreements to expand American liquefied natural gas exports to Europe, advanced the Vertical Corridor to reduce Europe’s dependence on Russian energy, strengthened our defense and security partnership with a critical NATO ally, and expanded opportunities for American businesses and investment throughout the region.

I am especially proud of the role our Embassy has played in strengthening American energy dominance, advancing economic cooperation, and ensuring that the United States remains the indispensable leader in Southeast Europe.

These accomplishments are a testament to President Trump’s bold leadership, Secretary Rubio’s commitment to American diplomacy, and the extraordinary men and women who serve our country every day.

I also want to address the recent allegations against me. These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity. I have dedicated my professional life to fighting for justice, standing up for what is right, and defending the values that make America exceptional. I will not allow false accusations to define my decades of public service.

My gratitude and respect for President Trump and Secretary Rubio remain unwavering. I am proud of what we accomplished together, and I will always be a loyal supporter of President Trump and his mission to Make America Great Again.

While my time as Ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement, and the country I love will never end.

It has been the honor of my lifetime to serve the United States of America. My deepest heartfelt appreciation to the people of Greece for their hospitality, partnership, and welcoming me with open arms. God bless President Trump, God bless our incredible diplomats and service members, and God bless the United States of America.

Last month, the CT Insurance Department officially approved an 11.3% average rate increase in 2027 for state-regulated, individual and small business health care coverage plans. Rx drug costs make up 30% of a Connecticut health care premium dollar. That amount has doubled since 2010. This trend screams out for action. 

Congress needs to pass the Lowering Drug Costs for American Families Act, a bill to empower Medicare to negotiate with pharmaceutical companies for lower Rx drug costs not just for Americans 65 and older, but for all Americans on employer-based plans and individual ACA marketplace plans (Access Health CT here in Connecticut). 

By lowering drug costs for working-age Americans, Congress would bring down health insurance premiums across the board. It's simple, and it will work.

Read more in my op-ed in the Day: https://t.co/ucwfATmo8p

text:
More Texans will now have access to federal Pell Grants to help pay for short-term job training programs.

Five Texas community colleges have been approved to offer eligible Workforce Pell programs, including Texas Southmost College in Brownsville. These programs will help students train for careers in fields like welding, health care, HVAC, and machining.

I supported expanding Pell Grant eligibility to include short-term trade and workforce training programs because students should have access to federal financial assistance whether they are pursuing a college degree or learning a skilled trade. This change will help more Texans gain the skills they need for good-paying jobs.

I encourage eligible Texans to explore these opportunities by completing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at https://t.co/8wv08KYFRt and contacting a participating college to learn more.

I also encourage other colleges across South Texas to seek approval for their workforce training programs so more students in our region can benefit from this federal assistance. Expanding access to affordable education and job training is important for our students, workers, and local economy.

https://t.co/0y4eqYXfWD

text:
October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

Women with dense breasts can be up to 4-5 times more likely to develop breast cancer than women without dense breasts. Dense breast tissue can also make cancer harder to detect on a mammogram.

As someone with dense breasts myself, I know how important it is for women to have access to the screening they need.

I’ve spent years fighting to expand access to additional testing because every woman deserves the information and care she needs to protect her health.

I led a congressional resolution to end the war in Iran.

Rep. Lauren Boebert (R-Colo.) says during her debate tonight that she never wanted to be at war with Iran and wants it to end, calling it “detrimental.”

“I never wanted us to be in war, at war, in Iran,” Boebert said. “This has been detrimental on many levels. I also will stand by and say that President Trump is the commander in chief, and he is not the first president to use force through his powers as commander in chief. Bill Clinton has done this in Kosovo. Obama in Libya … We do not have boots on the ground. I do agree that this is expensive. And I hear from Republicans, unaffiliated and Democrats that they want this to come to an end, and so do I.”

Moderator: “What are you doing to stop it?”

Boebert: “We are having conversations with the Department of War, with the president and his administration, on a regular basis about how to come to an end with this.”
“I hope that we come to a resolve very soon,” she added.

Earlier today, I was honored to host @RepMcGovern, Canadian Consul General @BernJordanCG, the Quebec Government Office’s Olivia Dion, and small businesses from both Vermont and Massachusetts in Brattleboro. We visited Allard Lumber in town and had a very important roundtable conversation about the U.S.-Canada relationship and the impacts of the trade war on folks on both sides of the border.
 
We heard repeatedly that businesses need stability. The constant and abrupt changes to our trade policy deprive businesses of the opportunity to plan ahead. It’s forcing them to take their attention away from serving their customers just to navigate all the red tape.
 
Nevertheless, the economic, community and personal ties between our two countries remain strong. Vermont and Canada have been interconnected for generations and we’re doing everything we can to keep it that way.

text: We all have plenty to be outraged by these days, but add this to the list:  through sheer lawlessness and brute force, Trump is trying to convert the historic East Potomac public golf course and park into a Epstein-class private club so he can host a PGA tournament in DC as another tribute to himself.  And don't be surprised if he ends up owning (or stealing) it on his way out the door.

quoted.text:
You saw the trees get cut down Saturday. Here's what you didn't see.

A political appointee gave the order at a closed-door October 5 meeting. NPS Deputy Director of Operations Frank Lands testified he was told by Greg Wischer, Interior's deputy chief of staff, to clear the trees as soon as "practicable." Crews moved over the holiday weekend, less than 24 hours after Friday's formal notice.

The judge isn't buying it. She said the real plan is being "developed outside of the agency, either through the White House or through private individuals coordinating with people at the White House."

Here's who those "private individuals" are:

• Tom Fazio is the designer Trump wants to redesign the course and build toward a Ryder Cup. Fazio Golf Design already has a signed agreement with the admin.

• Vanasse Hangen Brustlin, a Massachusetts engineering firm, quietly got a $389,355 contract for compliance work. Rep. Jared Huffman says it was awarded "without any public announcement or notice to Congress."

• A $49M construction contract is already posted as a govt forecast, bidding set to open 1/31/27. No company's been awarded it yet, but the price tag shows how big this project is.

The course didn't just become available. For years, National Links Trust (NLT), a nonprofit, ran it and kept it affordable. The admin was already dumping WH East Wing demolition debris there before Interior even took the lease back. A week later, Interior claimed NLT had defaulted (NLT disputes that) and canceled the lease 12/30. NLT has hired Williams & Connolly to fight it.

Friday at 4:55 p.m., NPS gave notice: 169 trees, Saturday — 16 times the judge's 10-tree limit. Lawyers later confirmed 430 were felled.

That's what Trump wants to turn into a "world-class" championship venue. Burgum claims it'll stay "affordable, highly discounted." Nobody buys that. A lawsuit argues this violates the 1897 law that created the park "for the recreation and the pleasure of the people" — meaning this may not just be unpopular. It may be illegal.

Reyes held a four-hour hearing, furious, and said the govt had lost all credibility.

Reyes has barred further cutting and is forcing DOJ to give three days' notice before touching this course again. Good. Not enough, but something.

#DemsUnited

text:
Over the summer, we learned that several servicemembers and civilians who worked at Fort Meade tragically died by suicide. One loss of life is one too many – and that is why I am committed to doing everything we can to make sure everyone at the Fort has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again. Here is an update on that work:

✔️In last year’s defense bill, I worked with colleagues to secure a provision requiring U.S. Cyber Command and the Cyber Mission Force to hire mental health professionals with security clearances at their operating locations. 

✔️I am now leading my Maryland delegation and Armed Services colleagues to help secure $11 million in funding needed to ensure full funding of this provision.

✔️I am also committed to working alongside U.S. Cyber Command to bring additional mental health resources to Fort Meade. I’m working to rectify the reporting requirements and include civilian employees in DoD’s suicide data, especially at installations like Fort Meade where civilian and uniformed officers work side by side on the same projects.

✔️Finally, I am working to address delays with the transfer of mental health licenses from out of state. During conversations with mental health professionals, I heard that the transfer of licenses can take several months to almost a year before these professionals can begin practicing in Maryland and on military bases. At the state level, I am working with partners, including @SenatorDawnGile and Secretary Ed Rothstein of the @MdVeterans, to address delays and barriers to military-connected mental health professionals transferring or obtaining professional licensure in Maryland.

This is just the beginning – and structurally addressing the gaps in mental health services and availability will be an ongoing effort. I will continue to keep you posted as we move this work forward together.

text:
The future of New Hampshire agriculture and food is in good hands! 🐄

I loved meeting the young Granite Staters of NH 4-H at the Sandwich Fair. They spend all year caring for their animals, and their pride and hard work were on full display in every barn and show ring. Every 4-H member pledges their head, heart, hands, and health to their club, community, country, and world, and I saw that pledge in action.

I also met so many of the people who make this fair so special: the local vendors, crafters, food makers, and small businesses who who put in long hours to share their work with their neighbors.

The costs of fuel, feed, equipment, and everyday living keep climbing, and it gets harder every year to keep a farm or small business in the family.

I'll keep fighting so our family farms and family-owned small businesses can thrive for generations to come. 🇺🇸
